criticalExposures.title: Unauthenticated Grafana console
criticalExposures.description: The Grafana administrative console is reachable from the public internet and accepts anonymous dashboard queries. A misconfigured anonymous role exposes datasource metadata and query results.
criticalExposures.evidence:
HTTP/2 200 OK
server: grafana
set-cookie: grafana_session=...
GET /api/datasources -> 200
GET /api/health -> {"database":"ok"}
criticalExposures.remediation: Disable anonymous access, require SSO through the corporate identity provider, and restrict the console to the VPN egress range. Rotate datasource credentials after applying the change.

criticalExposures.title: Public bucket exposes customer exports
criticalExposures.description: An S3 bucket used for nightly customer data exports allows anonymous ListBucket and GetObject. Object names follow the customer account identifier and export date.
criticalExposures.evidence:
aws s3 ls s3://mrc-backups-prod -> PRE 2026-11-18/
GET /mrc-backups-prod/2026-11-18/customer-exports.zip -> 200
x-amz-request-id: 8F3A...
criticalExposures.remediation: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level, replace the bucket policy with an explicit deny for anonymous principals, and confirm the retention policy for affected exports.

criticalExposures.title: Admin API key exposed in public bundle
criticalExposures.description: A privileged API key is embedded in the production JavaScript bundle served by the wealth application. The key grants read access to customer portfolio metadata.
criticalExposures.remediation: Revoke and rotate the exposed key, move the integration behind a server-side proxy, and add secret scanning to the frontend build pipeline.

criticalExposures.title: Kubernetes dashboard reachable without auth
criticalExposures.description: The Kubernetes dashboard is exposed to the internet and grants anonymous read access to namespace metadata. Workload secrets are not visible, but service topology is.
criticalExposures.remediation: Disable anonymous authentication, front the dashboard with the corporate identity proxy, and restrict network access to the platform team.

criticalExposures.title: Wildcard DNS takeover risk
criticalExposures.description: A wildcard DNS record points at a third-party edge provider without a verified ownership record. An attacker who claims the unbound hostname can serve content under the insurance brand.
criticalExposures.evidence:
dig CNAME random.claims.meridian-pay.com
-> unclaimed-vendor-edge.net
TXT ownership: missing
criticalExposures.remediation: Remove the dangling wildcard record, confirm the provider binding, and add subdomain-takeover monitoring to the DNS change workflow.
